mst.title: Maestro
mst.q.empty: No songs yet. Use + Add songs.
mst.pl.delInfo: The playlist and its song list are removed. This can't be undone.
mst.pl.gap.help: Seconds of silence before the next song starts when the queue moves on by itself. off = start right away.
mst.pv.instSync.help: Waits for the band player to start, then follows it, so the preview plays along with your performance. Mute the parts you play yourself.
mst.pv.noStemsHint: Pick a song in the queue to see its stems.
mst.status.noFiles: No songs in the folder yet.
mst.lib.empty: No songs found. Put .mid files in the folder, then Rescan.
mst.set.transpose.help: Shifts every note up or down in semitones (12 = one octave). Use it to move a song into the summoned instrument's playable range.
mst.set.hold.help: Adds to or subtracts from how long each note is held, in milliseconds. Positive makes notes ring longer (more sustain); negative cuts them shorter. 0 = each note's exact written length.
mst.set.tempo.help: Playback speed as a percent of the song's own tempo. 100 = original; higher is faster, lower is slower. In an ensemble the tempo is set by the ensemble instead.
mst.set.maxpoly.help: Caps how many notes may sound at once. When exceeded, the oldest (or the lowest within a chord) notes are dropped. off = no cap — lower it if dense passages overwhelm the instrument.
mst.set.restrike.help:
When the same pitch repeats, it is released this many ms before being struck again — including back-to-back notes — so each repeat registers as a new note. off = release exactly at the re-press, which makes fast same-pitch runs drop at the LISTENER in Network Sync mode.

Default 33 ms (inaudible). Raise it if dense same-pitch runs still drop for listeners.
mst.set.forceSustain.help:
Holds the sustain pedal down for the whole song, so each note rings until the next note on the same pitch.

Best for piano, guitar and bass. Leave it off for instruments that should re-articulate every note.
mst.set.applyTone.help:
Reads the GM instrument (program-change) on each MIDI track and applies the matching in-game tone/technique, switching live as the program changes. Off = every note plays Clean / Sustained.

Set the track's MIDI instrument to get each effect:
Guitar —
  • Overdriven Guitar → Overdrive
  • Distortion Guitar → Distortion
  • Electric Guitar (muted) → Muffled
  • Guitar Harmonics → Harmonics
  • any other guitar → Clean
Bass —
  • Slap Bass 1 / 2 → Slap
  • Synth Bass 1 / 2 → Overdrive
  • any other bass → Clean
Piano / drums / other → no effect (Clean / Sustained).

The effect is clamped to what the summoned instrument supports (e.g. a guitar has no Slap; on a bass, Distortion falls back to Overdrive).

Note: only ONE channel is read — the dominant one (the channel with the most notes). Program-changes on any other channel are ignored, so keep each stem to a single instrument channel for its tone to apply.
mst.set.relayTone.help: The game has a bug where your instrument's tone (e.g. guitar Overdrive/Distortion) often doesn't reach other players — they hear a plain, clean sound instead. When enabled, this sends your tone through an alternate path so it comes through correctly. Limitation: only listeners who also run Stellar will hear the corrected tone; players without the mod still hear it plain. Experimental — may stop working if the game is updated.
mst.set.netSync.help:
Builds the entire note timeline up front and plays it on a steady real-time clock instead of firing notes live.

Strongly recommended: it removes the per-note timing jitter other players hear, and it is required for Mute local, the on-screen key animation, and every ensemble sync option below.
mst.set.muteLocal.help.on:
Silences the instrument on your client only — everyone else still hears every note you play.

Use it to perform in a group without the sound in your own ears.
mst.set.muteLocal.help.off:
Silences the instrument on your client only.

Requires Network Sync mode — enable it first.
mst.set.keyviz.help:
Shows the on-screen key / note animation as the auto-player performs, so you can see what it is pressing in real time.

Requires Network Sync mode.
mst.monitorVol.help:
How loud you hear your OWN instrument through the ear-return (monitor) feed. Local only — it does not change what other players hear.

You may need to enable "Mute my local sound" to avoid hearing your instrument doubled.
mst.ens.sync.help:
Sync your playback with the group so everyone plays in time. How to use:

1. Enable this option.
2. Each player picks a track and presses Play — the status will show "waiting for ensemble…".
3. The party leader starts the ensemble, and everyone's playback syncs.

Note: once it has synced, you can leave the ensemble if you want.
Note: make sure every player uses the same Network Settings value — a mismatch can cause playback to go out of sync.
mst.ens.tempo.help:
On: the song is time-stretched to the ensemble's BPM and stays locked to it for the whole piece — no drift.

Off: only the first downbeat is aligned (count-in); if the song's BPM differs from the ensemble's, playback slowly drifts out of sync.

Requires Network Sync + Sync to ensemble.
mst.ens.autoAccept.help:
Automatically accepts incoming band-ensemble invitations, using the same reply the in-game Accept button sends.

The game's own preconditions apply: you must be in a team and have an instrument summoned.
mst.ens.footer: Join or start an ensemble in-game first; playback then locks to its grid.
mst.net.lookahead.desc: How far ahead notes are sent (stay under the receiver's ~500ms buffer).
mst.net.sendEvery.desc: Batch cadence — smaller = smoother local, more packets.
mst.net.tonelead.desc: How far ahead of the note the tone change is applied, in ms — raise it if a tone switch sounds one note late for listeners.
mst.pv.stoppedHint: Plays the selected queue song's stems.
mst.pv.offset.desc: Sync only: delay the backing to line up with a networked monitor (tune by ear). 0 = in sync with your local sound.
mst.pv.fileNaming.desc: Give a song's stems the same name, ending in the instrument in ( ):
mst.pv.fileNaming.dup: Each file gets its own row; duplicates like "(Bass 2)" are separate tracks (same bass sound).
mst.pv.fileNaming.select: Select any one in the queue — Preview loads the whole set.
mst.status.openFreePlay: Summon an instrument in Free Play first.
mst.status.queueEmpty: The queue is empty. Add songs from the Library.
mst.status.queueEmptyPreview: Add a song to the queue to preview it.
mst.status.noStems: No song files found for this song.

mst.link.hint: Enter the room code from the Maestro Link website.
mst.link.consent: Joining lets the room control this character's instrument and play songs. You can stop or leave at any time.
mst.link.how.title: How it works
mst.link.how.1: Create a room on the Maestro Link website, or get the code from your band leader.
mst.link.how.2: Enter the code above and press Join.
mst.link.how.3: The website picks songs and parts — your character plays its part by itself.
mst.link.err.notFound: Room not found or expired. Check the code and try again.
mst.link.err.version: This Maestro version doesn't match the room. Update Maestro and try again.
mst.link.err.closed: The Maestro Link room was closed.
mst.link.err.kicked: You were removed from the Maestro Link room.
mst.link.err.replaced: This character joined the room from another session.
mst.link.err.loggedOut: Disconnected from Maestro Link: you logged out. Press Join to rejoin the room.
mst.link.warn.bandView: Band view is closed — open free play to perform.
mst.link.warn.notSynced: Waiting for the game's server clock…
mst.link.warn.stopped: You stopped your part. It comes back with the next song.
